```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(framework)
scaffold()
```

The `save_*()` functions write tables, figures, models, and reports to the
folders in `settings.yml` and record each one in `framework.db`, so
`result_list()` can show what the project has produced. Run notebook 02 first:
this one reads `inputs.final.bp_long`.

```{r}
bp_long <- data_read("inputs.final.bp_long")
```

## Tables

Mean systolic pressure with a 95% confidence interval, by arm and visit.
`mean_ci()` comes from `functions/bp_helpers.R`.

```{r}
sbp_by_visit <- bp_long |>
  group_by(treatment, visit_number) |>
  reframe(mean_ci(systolic_bp)) |>
  mutate(across(c(mean, lower, upper), \(x) round(x, 1)))
sbp_by_visit
```

`save_table()` writes CSV by default. Look for the path in the message; the
folder is created on first use.

```{r}
save_table(sbp_by_visit, "sbp_by_visit")
```

Other formats: `xlsx` (needs writexl), `rds`, and `parquet` (needs arrow).

```{r}
save_table(sbp_by_visit, "sbp_by_visit", format = "xlsx")
save_table(sbp_by_visit, "sbp_by_visit", format = "parquet")
```

## Figures

The figure the tour is about: mean systolic pressure over visits, by arm. The
intervention arm falls visit by visit while control stays flat.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5
sbp_plot <- ggplot(sbp_by_visit, aes(visit_number, mean, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), position = position_dodge(width = 0.2)) +
  geom_line(position = position_dodge(width = 0.2)) +
  labs(
    title = "Systolic pressure falls over visits in the intervention arm",
    x = "Visit",
    y = "Mean systolic pressure (mmHg, 95% CI)",
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
sbp_plot
```

`save_figure()` takes a ggplot (or saves the last plot when `plot = NULL`).
Size is in inches.

```{r}
save_figure(sbp_plot, "sbp_trajectory", width = 7, height = 4.5)
save_figure(sbp_plot, "sbp_trajectory", format = "pdf", width = 7, height = 4.5)
```

Base graphics work too: draw the plot, then call `save_figure()` with a name.

```{r}
hist(bp_long$systolic_change, breaks = 30,
     main = "Change in systolic pressure from first visit", xlab = "mmHg")
save_figure(name = "sbp_change_histogram", width = 6, height = 4)
```

## Models

A mixed model of systolic pressure over visits, with a random intercept per
participant. `save_model()` stores the fitted object as RDS.

```{r}
bp_model <- lme4::lmer(
  systolic_bp ~ visit_number * treatment + age + sex + (1 | participant_id),
  data = bp_long
)
save_model(bp_model, "sbp_mixed_model")
```

The saved model reads back as the same object.

```{r}
reloaded <- readRDS("outputs/models/sbp_mixed_model.rds")
lme4::fixef(reloaded)
```

## Notebooks and reports

`save_notebook()` renders a Quarto document and saves the HTML to
`outputs/notebooks/`. Here it renders the short report in
`docs/bp-summary.qmd`, which reads the table and figure saved above.

```{r}
save_notebook("docs/bp-summary.qmd")
```

`save_report()` copies a finished file into `outputs/reports/` under a new
name, for example the version you sent to the study team.

```{r}
save_report("outputs/notebooks/bp-summary.html", name = "bp-summary-2026-11")
```

## What's been saved

`result_list()` reads the results table in `framework.db`. Each result is
named by its path, with a hash and timestamps.

```{r}
result_list()
```

Filter by type.

```{r}
result_list(type = "figure")[, c("name", "updated_at")]
```

## capture_output()

`capture_output()` runs an expression and returns its console output, its
value, and whether it errored, instead of printing. Handy for logging a model
summary.

```{r}
captured <- capture_output(print(summary(bp_model)$coefficients[, 1:2]))
captured$status
head(captured$console_output, 4)
```

An error doesn't stop the notebook; it comes back in `result`.

```{r}
failed <- capture_output(stop("model did not converge"))
failed$status
conditionMessage(failed$result)
```

## Scratch files

`scratch_capture()` dumps an object to `scratch/` (gitignored) for a quick
look outside R. Data frames become TSV and vectors become text; the file name
comes from the object name.

```{r}
high_readings <- bp_long |> filter(systolic_bp >= 160) |> select(participant_id, visit_number, systolic_bp)
scratch_capture(high_readings)
scratch_capture(unique(bp_long$site_name), name = "site_names")
scratch_capture(bp_model, name = "sbp_model_snapshot", to = "rds")
list.files("scratch")
```

`scratch_clean()` empties the top of `scratch/`.

```{r}
scratch_clean()
list.files("scratch")
```
